title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: In a system built around a language model, what is the clearest difference between a workflow and an agent?

options.text: A workflow calls the model once, while an agent calls it many times
A workflow uses no tools, while an agent is the one that uses tools
In a workflow the code sets the steps, while in an agent the model does
A workflow needs a person to approve each step, while an agent does not

items.stem: A makerspace assistant handles every booking request the same way. The program looks up the machine's free slots, then asks the model to write a reply offering those slots, then sends the reply. The model never chooses which step comes next. How should this design be described?

options.text: A workflow, because the program fixes the order of the steps
An agent, because the model is called and writes a reply
An agent, because it looks up information using a tool
A workflow, because the model is called only one time

items.stem: For the part of the assistant that confirms a booking, the steps are always the same: check the slot is free, write the booking, send a confirmation. Cost per request matters to the team. Which design is the better choice for this part?

options.text: An agent, so the model can choose whichever steps it likes
An agent, because agents are always more accurate than code
A workflow, because workflows never need to call a model
A workflow, because known steps need no model decisions

items.stem: Suppose every model call costs about the same. A fixed workflow answers a question with exactly 2 model calls. An agent answering the same kind of question makes 3 tool requests and then a final answer, so 4 model calls. Over 100 questions, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow?
Give one situation, in a few words, in which an agent is a better choice than a fixed workflow.

The team must pick a design for the whole assistant. Booking follows the same steps every time. Questions about the machine manuals vary a lot: some need one page, some need several pages, and some need a calendar check too. Which design is the most defensible for a small budget?

options.text: One agent for everything, so the design stays simple and flexible
A fixed workflow for booking, and an agent for open-ended manual questions
A fixed workflow for everything, with one branch written for each question
An agent for booking, and a fixed workflow for open-ended manual questions
